The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and government regulators on Thursday (November 5, 2026) issued a warning about cyber-attacks targeting industrial coolers and fridges.

The warning acknowledged that hackers were targeting vulnerabilities in unpatched or internet-linked refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities.

Gaining control of these systems would enable hackers to adjust temperatures to dangerous extremes or run unauthorised defrost cycles, leading to the spoilage of inventory or even fire hazards.

The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Health and Human Services (HHS), U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the Department of Transportation (DOT) warned organisations about “ongoing cyber threat activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems.”

The U.S. FBI-issued factsheet recommended that organisations with cold storage facilities de-link control system devices from the internet, enhance password security, apply patches to keep systems updated, and replace legacy devices that no longer receive security updates.

The notice came shortly after cyber attacks led to huge amounts of food waste across European supermarket franchises, where some fridge temperatures were raised as high as 50 degrees Celsius in October.

The parents of a 13-year-old girl have sued Google claiming she planned a potential suicide and funeral using its AI technology on a school-issued computer.

Filed Monday in a California court, the complaint is the first known case accusing Google of negligence related to AI integrations on Chromebooks, the tech giant's low-cost laptops used by millions of students in the United States and around the world.

The teenager was not able to access Google's Gemini app, nor OpenAI's ChatGPT, because they were blocked by her school. She was nonetheless still able to use Google's search engine, which contains AI-powered tools.

Those features were notably not among the tools that Google announced this week will be disabled by default for students.

"Schools should turn search off and keep it off until Google removes AI mode from search or ensures that every single student is always safe when they're interacting with AI," Andrew Liddell, one of the family's attorneys, told AFP on Thursday.

A major cyberattack targeted cold storage facilities of France’s national blood agency , Etablissement Francais du Sang (EFS), after hackers breached systems to remotely heat freezers holding donor blood samples and plasma.

The incident was reported between November 1 and 2, when unknown bad actors compromised Coolworld, a key refrigeration maintenance contractor for EFS.

They reprogrammed cold storage units, typically kept at a freezing −30°C to safely preserve blood products, by pushing temperature settings up to 110°C (230°F).

However, an on-duty technician noticed this abnormal overnight temperature spike on monitoring systems, and averted the damage. Rapid emergency protocols allowed technical teams to intervene before permanent damage affected the inventory.

France’s Ministry of Health confirmed that the breach was contained with zero operational disruption to hospital supplies or transfusion services.

While the EFS initially reported that the impacted containers held routine health-monitoring blood samples, official statements later confirmed that frozen plasma meant for medical transfusions was also stored within the affected refrigeration units.

headline: As New Delhi’s air turns toxic again, people complain of unaffordable air purification products
body: Despite observations from the Delhi High Court and recommendations from a Parliamentary Standing Committee to reduce the 18% GST on purifiers and HEPA filters to 5%, the GST Fitment Committee maintained the 18% levy

Winter is just getting started, but the air quality in India’s national capital has already deteriorated to ‘very poor’ category, and the city is bracing for a harsh, polluted winter. Against this backdrop, a survey of over 51,000 respondents across 212 districts in the country paints a bleaker picture.

According to a survey by LocalCircles, around 89% of respondents said that the government has not done enough to make pollution-coping products affordable, with 78% stating that official measures have been inadequate. Nearly 88% of air purifier users have urged the government to standardise replacement filters to improve availability and lower costs.

Delhi’s Air Quality Index (AQI) touched 331 on November 3, 2026, prompting authorities to invoke Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP).

Beyond Delhi, real-time rankings placed 22 of the world’s 25 most polluted cities in India, with Mumbai also ranking third globally among major metropolises. Amid heightened respiratory health concerns, air purifiers have transitioned from niche luxury products into essential household appliances.

However, severe supply shortages of model-specific HEPA replacement filters during peak winter leave many appliances unusable. “Current Indian Standards and recent Quality Control Orders focus exclusively on electrical safety and clean air delivery rates rather than filter interchangeability, [making] consumers unable to locate specific model filters [and forcing them] to purchase entirely new devices,” the survey said.

Affordability also remains another key hurdle. Despite observations from the Delhi High Court and recommendations from a Parliamentary Standing Committee to reduce the 18% Goods and Services Tax (GST) on purifiers and HEPA filters to 5%, the GST Fitment Committee maintained the 18% levy.

The story so far: Early morning on October 29, many customers at Binance, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the world, began receiving messages that their accounts were being unexpectedly emptied. What followed, over the course of just about 20 minutes, was the biggest crypto hack in history, with more than $6 billion worth being stolen. By November 2, Binance had replaced 100% of the stolen amount to customers. The search for the culprit and recovery process still continues, but the customer impact has been mitigated in a remarkably short time.

Cryptocurrency transactions involve a multi-rung authentication involving public keys as well as private keys that are held by each user. According to Binance, a preliminary investigation points to a “compromised” laptop belonging to one of its engineers that could have allowed the hacker to submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.
